---
title: "Field-epidemiology training: the business case"
description: "A discrete choice experiment and cost model supporting a World Bank business case for scaling field-epidemiology training."
---

Outbreak detection depends on trained field epidemiologists, and training them is
expensive enough that scale-up decisions get made on intuition. This project built
the evidence for one: a discrete choice experiment on what makes a training
programme attractive to the people who would enrol, combined with a cost model for
what different scale-up paths would take.

The two halves matter together. A programme that is cheap per graduate but that
nobody wants to join does not produce graduates. The choice experiment prices the
programme features that drive enrolment; the cost model prices delivering them.

The result is [STEPS](/tools/steps/), which lets a planner change the scale-up
assumptions and see the consequences, rather than reading a single recommended
scenario.

Developed with the World Bank.
